Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed on so we have everything captured:

1) What you need from us
- Export of audit log entries showing who accessed what data and when (user/service principal, action, resource, timestamp, IP, auth method).
- Export formats: NDJSON preferred, CSV also accepted for ingestion into your SIEM.
- Retention policy and proof of retention for the past 13 months, and options for extending retention to 24 months.
- Evidence of role-based access controls and the ability to filter logs by customer account and by event type.

2) Deliverables from Redwood
- Sample export (anonymized) in NDJSON + CSV schema describing the fields.
- Short doc describing retention policy, retention export process, and admin access controls.
- Steps for secure transfer and verification (S3 presigned URL or secure Drive link) and an agreed ETA.

3) Timeline / next steps
- Aditya will attach a sample NDJSON + schema by EOD tomorrow (we aim 6/11).
- Sara to confirm whether you need logs down to the token-level (we typically log request/response metadata but do not persist unredacted model outputs by default; we can discuss dedicated/private options if you need that).
- Ben will review for compliance questions specific to your audit team and join any follow-ups if needed.

Attachments: redwood_audit_log_sample.ndjson (anonymized stub), redwood_audit_log_schema.csv

If that aligns with your notes, we'll push the sample and policy doc tomorrow.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. That matches our conversation. A few clarifying items from the audit team before you send the sample: 

- We need to confirm whether the "user" field in your logs maps to an internal Redwood username/service account or to our customer-facing identity (i.e., does the log include our end-user id). Ideally we can filter by our customer account id only.
- Please confirm retention defaults and whether there is a separate export for admin/operator actions vs. application-level events.
- For redaction: we cannot accept logs that contain unredacted PII. If the sample contains user identifiers, please pseudonymize or hash them.
- Delivery method: S3 presigned link is preferred (we will provide a short-lived ingestion bucket if needed).

If you can include a short README with the sample describing each field and its possible values (especially the auth_method and action enums), that would be great.

Thanks — aim to review the sample same day you send it.

Sara

Hi Sara — attaching the anonymized sample and the schema as discussed. Notes on the export and fields below.

Attachment stubs: redwood_audit_log_sample.ndjson, redwood_audit_log_schema.csv

Quick field notes (README):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC for the event (e.g., 2026-06-10T22:34:12Z)
- customer_account_id: Redwood customer identifier (filterable)
- actor_id: pseudonymized internal user/service principal id (we hash internal usernames for external evidence)
- action: enum (READ, WRITE, EXPORT, ADMIN_UPDATE, AUTH_SUCCESS, AUTH_FAILURE)
- resource: resource path (model_id, dataset_id, or route)
- ip_address: source IP (we can truncate/obfuscate if required)
- auth_method: e.g., api_key, oauth, sso, service_account
- request_id: unique per request for cross-correlation

Retention and exports: 
- Default retention for audit logs is 13 months for Hosted accounts. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can support configurable retention up to 24 months (contract/architecture dependent).
- We do not retain unredacted model outputs in audit logs by default. Request/response metadata is included per above. For customers that require full content retention we recommend Private deployment with explicit contractual controls.

Delivery options:
- We can provide an S3 presigned PUT or a secure Drive link (we used presigned S3 for large exports). Files can be NDJSON (newline delimited JSON) or CSV.

Let me know if you want a sample with masked PII (we included hashed actor_id in this sample). If that looks good I can upload to a presigned S3 link tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Thanks Aditya — the sample looks good and the README answers most of our questions. Confirming a couple final items so we can sign off with audit: 

- actor_id hashing approach: acceptable as long as hashing is one-way and you can prove the hash algorithm. Please include algorithm name (e.g., SHA256) in the README.
- Admin/operator actions: we need a separate flag on events for "admin" vs "application" so our audit tooling can surface privilege escalations. If that exists, note the field name.
- Retention: 13 months default is fine for now; please include the contractual path to extend to 24 months (who to contact on renewals/ops).

If you can provide the S3 presigned link with the files and README, we'll ingest and run it through our SIEM. After ingestion we'll confirm if any additional extracts are needed. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sara
